articles.paper: BlinkMimic: Training a Humanoid Motion Tracker in Minutes on a Single GPU
articles.title: When smaller batches weaken Muon’s descent

blocks.text: BlinkMimic trains motion tracking for a simulated Unitree G1 through a differentiable world model. The appendix uses a local quadratic model to explain the batch-size knee, treating momentum as signal plus noise with entrywise variance inversely proportional to batch size B. [1]

blocks.label: Appendix A.4 heuristic; H is the local Hessian and the inner product is Frobenius

blocks.text: The appendix treats the curvature term as approximately constant. As B falls, progress per step shrinks rapidly when alignment approaches the curvature cost. After fitting at B=1,024, the preregistered prediction at B=512 was 2,280–2,630 iterations; one seed took 2,301. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The full recipe reaches three consecutive clean checkpoints in 3.4 minutes on average on an RTX 4090 (40 LAFAN1 clips, four replicas each, mean return at least 0.82; timing excludes offline evaluation). This is a whole-recipe result, and the Adam swap holds the recipe’s step size and batch fixed. [1]

articles.paper: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
articles.authors: Jie Wang · Tong Zhu · JiaHao Kuang · Zhe Xu · Yunkai Chai · Dehong Zheng · Yu Cheng · Tao Ji · ZhouHan Lin · Qi Zhang · Bowen Zhou
articles.title: Separating the optimal loss surface from tuning penalties

blocks.text: ArchSpace builds compute ladders for Qwen3.5 and OLMo3. Let M denote training FLOPs per token and D the token count. The fitted surface is minimized at fixed C=MD. For each model–budget pair, learning rate and batch are swept, and their best measured loss fits the base surface. [2]

blocks.label: Eq. (3); coupling exponent 1 recovers the additive form. The loss penalty for off-optimum hyperparameters is fitted separately
Empirical parameterization; the first term lets the best learning rate shift with batch size

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: With coefficients frozen, extrapolations along the fitted compute-optimal path up to ten times the largest fit budget yield Table 4 loss MAPE of 0.32%; the base surface alone gives 0.33%. These runs stay within the original tokens-per-parameter range. The authors ran a separate hyperparameter search for long training at about 130–160 tokens per parameter. [2]

articles.title: Hera adds a Muon baseline for nonlinear forecasting
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted 2026-03-02; v2 submitted 2026-11-11 06:59 EST · announced Nov 13
articles.evidence: Compared v1/v2; read the v2 experiment and appendix

blocks.text: V2 adds one-step Lorenz–63 forecasting. Three softmax-attention layers read five successive states and a fixed readout predicts the next state. Hera updates two matrices independently in whitened coordinates, while Hera-PSD ties them together. [3,4]

blocks.label: Experimental parameterization; Muon and AdamW update the raw attention matrices

blocks.text: The train, validation, and test splits are consecutive blocks of 500 examples from one trajectory. Each method screens 44 configurations, with validation MSE used to select the long-run configuration. The table gives mean test MSE over five fresh initializations after 4,096 full-batch updates. [3]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The new results come from one dynamical-system trajectory. The finite-sample guarantee uses planted linear models and independent samples, and the table does not control for time per step. [3]

articles.authors: George Cazenavette · Angelina Quan · Giannis Daras · Antonio Torralba · Vincent Sitzmann
articles.title: Synthetic data target class-conditional coverage

blocks.text: A frozen feature extractor defines attraction to real data and repulsion from other synthetic examples, optimizing images and their augmentations directly. On ImageNet-1k with 10 images per class, noise initialization and hard-label ResNet-18 training, the best MoCo-v3 variant reaches 27.0% test accuracy versus 11.7% for the strongest noise-initialized baseline. Coverage is feature-space dependent, and the paper reports same-encoder evaluation separately. [5]

title: Muon’s batch-size knee and pretraining beyond the fitted budget
subtitle: BlinkMimic · ArchSpace · Hera · Consistency Models
intro: This issue picks up two scaling comparisons from the November 13 arXiv announcements and reads the new Muon baseline in Hera. The classic revisits Consistency Models and explains one-step generation through a shared probability-flow trajectory.

classic.title: Predicting a shared trajectory endpoint in one pass
classic.authors: Yang Song · Prafulla Dhariwal · Mark Chen · Ilya Sutskever
classic.dateNote: First arXiv posting 2023-03-02 ET; read the ICML 2023 version
classic.question: At fixed student capacity, how should the time grid be allocated to balance solver error at low noise against pairwise residuals from finite training?

blocks.text: Score SDE (2021) sends a high-noise sample back to the data end along a deterministic probability-flow ODE, typically requiring multiple network evaluations. Consistency Models learn each trajectory’s endpoint directly, with the identity map at the low-noise boundary. Let t be the Gaussian noise standard deviation and pₜ the perturbed marginal. [8,10]

blocks.tex: p_t=p_{\rm data}*\mathcal N(0,t^2I),\quad \dot x_t=-t\nabla\log p_t(x_t),\quad f(x_t,t)=x_\epsilon,\quad f(x,\epsilon)=x
blocks.label: Sections 2–3; f is constant along each trajectory

blocks.tex: f_\theta(x,t)=c_{\rm skip}(t)x+c_{\rm out}(t)F_\theta(x,t),\qquad c_{\rm skip}(\epsilon)=1,\quad c_{\rm out}(\epsilon)=0
blocks.label: The skip connection enforces the boundary condition
Algorithm 2: a teacher score and ODE solver take a step from the later time to the earlier time. The target network uses EMA and stopped gradients
Theorem 1: zero distillation loss, Lipschitz dependence on input, and uniform solver local error of order p+1. The target is the teacher’s empirical ODE
Algorithm 3 pairs perturbations using shared Gaussian noise. This replaces the teacher step, with the theoretical connection made in the fine-grid limit

blocks.text: In Table 1 on CIFAR-10, CD reaches FID 3.55 and 2.93 with one and two network evaluations. NFE counts network calls per sample, and FID compares feature distributions of generated and real images. [8]
